what: Concurrency and span facts re-derived from the archived run traces by `harness probe concurrency`.

derivation.leg_start: receipts/dispatch.jsonl — the PostToolUse dispatch receipt, hook-attested and append-only
derivation.leg_end: t0/trials.jsonl — the last T0 trial inside the dispatch's own window. A LANDMARK NEAR THE END, not the end: every figure derived through it is a lower bound.
derivation.not_used: result-file mtimes. The traces were copied, so every mtime is the copy time; a measurement built on them is fabricated, not approximate.
derivation.note: No archived run has a legs.jsonl — leg completion records did not exist when these runs were taken. That is why every leg below is `lower` and every speedup is refused.
derivation.leg_end_inner: t0/trials.jsonl is ALSO kept as an inner end alongside any leg-record end, not only as a fallback. An interval that closes at a T0 trial is one the leg provably occupied; one that closes at an ingest may have been closed by somebody other than the leg. Overlap is reported both ways and the acceptance answer is taken from the inner form when it covers every leg.
derivation.regenerated: 2026-08-17 — the instrument gained the inner-interval fields (max_concurrent_inner, ends_disputed, inner_ended_at, end_lag_ms) after a dial-1 run reported max_concurrent 2 because one of its legs had been ingested by hand 250.8s late. EVERY FIGURE ALREADY RECORDED HERE IS UNCHANGED: all nine entries re-derive the same max_concurrent, the same bound, the same instant and the same acceptance answer, and on all nine the inner figure equals the outer one. Only the added fields moved, which is why this is a regeneration and not a new measurement.

d1.question: did ≥2 scopes ever build concurrently?
d1.answer: yes — proven, and by a lower bound, which is the safe direction
d1.strongest_evidence: headless-shipped round 1: 4 legs open simultaneously at 2026-08-16T02:16:34.692Z, 6/6 legs with an end landmark
d1.note: Truncated legs are subintervals of the true legs, so overlap over them UNDER-counts. A lower bound of 4 settles ≥2 without needing the exact figure.

d3.question: does wall-clock beat the Phase-2 baseline by ≥30%?
d3.reason: There is no sequential arm anywhere in this archive. Every archived run was executed by the post-Phase-3 fan-out scheduler, so there is nothing for a fan-out to be measured against. Phase 2's recorded baseline is structural — line counts, inventories and a green suite — not a run, which is what RESULT-v2 means by 'No number about v2.0's cost or wall-clock appears anywhere in this repo'. No number is entered here, because a number derived from these traces would be a comparison of a run against itself.

what_would_produce_one.design: the same feature built twice, changing exactly one variable: maxParallelScopes 1 vs 4
what_would_produce_one.measure: BUILD-phase span only (`probe concurrency --round <N>` → launches[].span_ms). Whole-run wall-clock dilutes the ratio toward zero, because ORIENT/ANALYZE/WIRE/EVAL/QA are sequential in both arms.
what_would_produce_one.requires: the fan-out dial must be reachable first — `maxParallelScopes` is read by the orchestrator and declared in no contract, so the sequential arm cannot currently be requested.
what_would_produce_one.precondition: both arms must produce legs.jsonl rows for every leg, or the instrument will refuse the speedup exactly as it does here.

d3.cost_note: Cost is not derivable either: no archived run root carries an agent-call journal, so no cost_usd row exists to aggregate.
